findings.description: The members API now requires '../../lib/magic-link/magic-link', but the file was not renamed and still exists as MagicLink.js. Loading MembersAPI throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on a case-sensitive filesystem, so member signup and magic-link auth cannot start. Restore the require to MagicLink or rename the file and update the remaining PascalCase callers together.
findings.title: Members API requires missing kebab-case MagicLink

findings.description: init() now requires '../email-service/email-event-storage' and '../email-service/email-event-processor', but those modules were not part of this rename and still exist as EmailEventStorage.js and EmailEventProcessor.js. On a case-sensitive filesystem, EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND before event storage or processing can run. Point both requires back at the existing PascalCase filenames.
findings.failureMode: MODULE_NOT_FOUND when EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init loads EmailEventStorage and EmailEventProcessor
findings.title: Email analytics requires unrenamed event modules

findings.description: The rename also stripped semicolons from the first ten require statements in members-api.js (lines 1-4 and 6-10), while the rest of the file keeps them. Mandate 19 requires explicit semicolons on every JavaScript statement. Those lines will fail the repository semicolon check even though Node can parse them via ASI. Restore the semicolons on each of those requires.
findings.failureMode: Repository semicolon mandate violated on changed require statements; lint rejects the file
findings.title: Members API requires dropped required semicolons

findings.description: The public pool now uses vmImage macOS-15, but the macOS step still runs `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` while its display name was changed to “Use XCode 16.4.0”. The macOS-15 hosted image does not contain Xcode_15.2.0.app; Xcode 16.4 is installed at /Applications/Xcode_16.4.app and /Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app. xcode-select therefore exits non-zero and the public macOS build fails before compilation. Update the selector to the 16.4 path.
findings.failureMode: public macOS jobs fail at xcode-select after the image bump to macOS-15
findings.title: macOS-15 image still selects Xcode 15.2

findings.description: The internal pool now uses image macOS-15, but its macOS step still selects `/Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` while the display name was updated to “Use XCode 16.4.0”. That bundle is absent from the macOS-15 image (16.4 is at /Applications/Xcode_16.4.app or /Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app), so xcode-select fails and the internal macOS build never starts. Select the 16.4 path.
findings.failureMode: internal macOS jobs fail at xcode-select after the image bump to macOS-15
findings.title: Internal macOS-15 image still selects Xcode 15.2

findings.description: original_identifier now reads config.bundle as a string instead of the top-level identifier string. Bundle is an object, so as_str() is always None and mobile option server-address files are never written: write_options fails with "app configuration is missing an identifier" even when tauri.conf.json has a valid identifier. The deleted lookup was config.get("identifier").
findings.title: Bundle identifier source lookup never matches

findings.description: The schema gate now requires the config path extension to be both json and json5. No path satisfies that, so invalid tauri.conf.json/json5 files skip validation and no longer exit(1). The previous condition was a logical OR.
findings.title: JSON schema validation is unreachable

findings.description: merge_with still builds the merged JSON and sets TAURI_CONFIG, but it no longer writes that value back to config_metadata.inner. The Xcode script later constructs AppInterface from that same loaded config (xcode_script.rs:239), so CLI --config overrides passed through merge_with are ignored and the iOS compile uses the pre-merge settings. The removed assignment was config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value). Restore that assignment after the merge.
findings.title: merge_with no longer applies config patches

findings.description: GetAvailableSlotsResponse types fromUser.id as string, but the slots API and IGetAvailableSlots/IFromUser contract use numeric user ids. useAvailableSlots now returns this type, and EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes schedule.data into useAvailableTimeSlots, which requires IGetAvailableSlots. TypeScript rejects that assignment because string is not assignable to number, so the calendar view no longer typechecks and consumers cannot treat the returned user id as a number. Change fromUser.id to number to match IFromUser and the API payload.
findings.title: Slot response types user IDs as strings

findings.description: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn types availability.days as string[], but Prisma Availability.days is Int[] and getScheduleListItemData requires days: number[]. useAtomGetAllSchedules returns this type, and ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes each schedule into getScheduleListItemData. TypeScript rejects that call because string[] is not assignable to number[], so the schedule list no longer typechecks and weekday numbers are mis-typed. Change days to number[].
findings.title: Schedule list types weekday days as strings

findings.description: setupToolbarConstraints now pins toolbar.leadingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor while toolbar.trailingAnchor is pinned to the same bar's leadingAnchor. The right skeleton is placed at the container's trailing edge, so both horizontal anchors refer to a view that sits entirely outside the container's trailing side. When tab swiping is enabled, Auto Layout cannot give the real toolbar a positive width and the address bar collapses or conflicts. The leading anchor must stay equal to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor, as before this change.
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchor attached to the right skeleton

findings.description: The pageActionStack rename left updateToolbarLayout concatenating browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews twice and dropping trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews. updateActionStack sets alpha to 0 on buttons that are not already in the stack, and only this list restores alpha to 1. After any animated or non-animated configure that adds trailing page actions (share, reader mode, reload), those buttons stay invisible. Restore trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews as the fourth term.
findings.title: Trailing page actions never fade in

findings.description: updateActionSpacing now sets hasPageActions from leadingPageActionStack instead of the renamed trailing page-action stack. The divider sits between the URL and trailing page actions, and its width is supposed to be browserActionsAddressBarDividerWidth only when that trailing stack has buttons. With only leading actions (or only trailing actions) the divider width is inverted: a gap appears beside an empty trailing side, or the divider collapses to zero while trailing buttons are present. Check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.title: Divider width follows the wrong page-action stack

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult loops with j <= keys_result->numkeys and writes slot_buffer[j], but slot_buffer is allocated for only numkeys ints and keys[] has only numkeys entries. Every cluster command with at least one key (GET, SET, MGET, SINTER, EVAL, and ASM getSlotFromCommand) therefore reads keys[numkeys] and writes one int past the buffer before returning. That is an out-of-bounds read of the key index and an out-of-bounds write on the main request path; the buffer is never read afterward. Fix the bound to j < numkeys and drop the unused allocation, using zmalloc/zfree if a buffer is actually required.
findings.failureMode: reachable crash or heap corruption on every cluster command with keys
findings.title: Slot extraction walks one past the key array

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the toolbar leading constraint was changed from leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor, while the trailing constraint still pins to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor. The right skeleton is laid out starting at the container's trailing edge, so both horizontal constraints now refer to that offscreen bar and conflict: the live toolbar no longer spans from the left skeleton's trailing edge to the right skeleton's leading edge and cannot lay out across the container. Restore the leading constraint to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor.
findings.title: Toolbar leading edge pinned to the right skeleton bar

findings.description: The pageActionStack rename was not applied to updateToolbarLayout. New trailing page-action buttons (reload, stop, reader mode, summarize) are still created with alpha 0, but the fade-in list now concatenates browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews twice and never includes trailingPageActionStack. On the main animated toolbar update path those buttons remain transparent and untappable; the non-animated else branch has the same omission. Restore trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews in that list.
findings.title: Trailing page actions stay invisible after rename

findings.description: updateActionSpacing used to show the location divider when the trailing page-action stack (pageActionStack) was non-empty. After the rename it checks leadingPageActionStack instead. The divider sits between the URL and the trailing actions, so a normal iPhone toolbar with only reload/reader-mode trailing actions and no leading share/translate actions collapses dividerWidthConstraint to 0, and leading actions alone incorrectly force the 4pt divider. Check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.title: Divider width follows the wrong page-action stack

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc 6 but seven objects follow: HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, and newobj. The helper allocates and consumes only argc arguments, so the propagated vector is HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 <field>. HSETEX arity is -6 and hsetexParseArgs requires a field/value pair after FIELDS numfields, so both the replica (processCommand arity check) and AOF replay (hsetexParseArgs) reject the command and never store the incremented value, while the primary already wrote it. newobj is also leaked: its refcount stays 1 because the rewrite never increments it, and decrRefCount(newobj) only releases the caller's reference, not a reference the rewrite never took. Change the count to 7 so the final value is included and its reference is owned by the command vector.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT rewrite drops the new field value

findings.description: hincrbyfloatCommand now calls hashTypeSet with only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE, dropping the HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL flag that the previous line passed. For an existing field with a TTL, hashTypeSet then clears that expiry: listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL) for LISTPACK_EX, and hfieldPersist() for hashtable encoding. HINCRBY still passes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, and tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl expects HINCRBYFLOAT to preserve HPTTL. After HSETEX/HPEXPIRE plus HINCRBYFLOAT, HTTL/HPTTL on the primary returns -1 and the field no longer expires. The later HSETEX KEEPTTL rewrite only affects what is propagated; it does not restore the TTL already removed from the local object. Restore HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this call.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT drops field TTL on the master

findings.description: original_identifier now reads the top-level `bundle` object and treats it as a string. Tauri v2 stores the app identifier at the root (`identifier`), and `bundle` is an object, so a normal tauri.conf.json yields None. write_options then fails with "app configuration is missing an identifier" before creating the mobile server-addr file, so Android/iOS CLI option handoff cannot start. Restore `config.get("identifier")`.
findings.title: Original identifier read from bundle object

findings.description: The extension check was changed from `||` to `&&`, so a path must be both `.json` and `.json5`. Every real config file fails that test, `config_schema_validator().iter_errors` is never called, and invalid tauri.conf.json/json5 values no longer exit(1). Restore the `||` so either extension is validated.
findings.title: Schema validation never runs

findings.description: merge_with still merges the patch into a local JSON value and sets TAURI_CONFIG, but the assignment that wrote the parsed result back to config_metadata.inner was removed. After the call, ConfigHandle still exposes the pre-merge Config. Android Studio and Xcode scripts call merge_with and then read that handle for devUrl, identifier, and bundle settings, so CLI config overrides are ignored for the remainder of the script. Restore `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value)?` after the merge.
findings.title: merge_with no longer updates loaded config

findings.description: The new schema parse statement is one line longer than rustfmt's max_width of 100. rustfmt --check rewrites it by breaking before `.expect`, so `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails. Wrap that call to match rustfmt.
findings.title: Schema parse line exceeds rustfmt width

findings.description: The replacement `extensions.insert` call is one line longer than rustfmt max_width 100. `rustfmt --check` rewrites it across multiple lines, so `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails. Break the method chain the same way rustfmt does.
findings.title: merge_with insert exceeds rustfmt width

findings.description: `POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite` is guarded with `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")`. RolesGuard treats the decorator as a minimum role (`TEAM_OWNER` < `TEAM_ADMIN` < `TEAM_MEMBER` via `hasMinimumRole`), so any team member passes and can create a verification token that `inviteMemberByToken` accepts as a join link. The sibling org invite controller and membership-create endpoint require `TEAM_ADMIN`, and the trpc createInvite handler requires `team.invite` with OWNER/ADMIN fallback. Change this decorator to `TEAM_ADMIN`. The new e2e that expects 403 for role MEMBER asserts the intended contract and currently fails because of this line.
findings.title: Team members can mint shareable invite links

findings.description: Newly created invites return `newToken.identifier` (`invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`) as `token`, while the stored secret is the hex `token` column and `inviteLink` is built from that secret. Signup and `/teams` look up `verificationToken.token` (`findUnique({ where: { token } })`, `inviteMemberByToken`, `acceptInvitationByToken`), so the API `data.token` cannot join anyone. The existing-token branch still returns `existingToken.token`, so the two response shapes disagree. Return `newToken.token` (or the local `token` variable), matching the pre-change return and the lookup branch.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of secret token

findings.description: `buildInviteLink` now returns `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=` when `isOrgContext` is true and the `/signup?token=&callbackUrl=` link otherwise. Base returned the teams link for non-org teams and the signup link for organizations and org sub-teams. A regular-team shareable link now sends invitees through org signup (signup treats a non-email identifier as an org invite only when the team is an org or sub-team), and an org/sub-team link goes to `/teams` and skips signup onboarding. Restore `if (!isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink`.
findings.title: Invite link branch is inverted for org vs team

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction. A normal reader-mode button tap dispatches showReaderMode, and BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions maps that display state to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction rather than toggleReaderMode. The page therefore is not switched into or out of reader mode; the tap instead tries to add the page to the reading list. Restore displayView: .readerMode.
findings.title: Reader-mode tap opens reading list

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry now returns false when readerModeState is .available and true for .active or .unavailable. The adjacent comment still says the button will be enabled after execution, and toolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped records this value as the Glean enabled extra. Tapping reader mode on an available page therefore records enabled=false, while closing an active reader-mode page records enabled=true. Restore the .available true / default false mapping.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry flag inverted

findings.description: On iPad (iOS 17+), OnboardingTests.tearDown returns before app.terminate() and super.tearDown() for every test, not just the skipped bottom-placement case. The app stays running and XCTest teardown is skipped, so later tests inherit the previous app state. Return only from the theme-reset branch, after terminate and super.tearDown.
findings.title: iPad onboarding teardown skips terminate

findings.description: Renaming `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` makes XCTest ignore it, so the iOS 17 reminders share path never runs. AccessibilityTestPlan still skips the old `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()` identifier, which no longer exists. Restore the `test` prefix (and update the skip entry if the method name must change).
findings.title: Reminders share test renamed off XCTest

findings.description: The nested UX struct that held buttonSize was deleted, and the close-button constraints now use the literal 40. Mandate 13 requires UI measurements to live in a nested UX struct rather than as implementation literals. Restore a private UX struct on DownloadToast and reference UX.buttonSize from these constraints.
findings.title: Download close button size is an inline magic number

findings.description: The added @MainActor @Sendable annotations make this function signature 128 characters, above the 125-character SwiftLint line_length warning required by mandate 2. Break the parameter list across lines so the file passes SwiftLint.
findings.title: Open-in-new-private-tab signature exceeds line length

findings.description: The atoms override now treats every @calcom/trpc and ../../trpc import as an error, but this refactor leaves import { QueryCell } from "@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell" in ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx. Previously the rule only matched @calcom/trpc/react, so those imports were allowed. Biome 2.3.10 lint of those files against this biome.json reports noRestrictedImports errors on both imports. yarn lint runs biome lint in @calcom/features, which includes the atoms tree, and the pre-commit hook lints staged atoms files with --error-on-warnings. Either check now fails. Keep the QueryCell imports legal, or move QueryCell out of trpc before widening the group.
findings.title: Biome ban now flags remaining atoms trpc imports

findings.description: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn is the type useAtomGetAllSchedules assigns to atoms/schedules/all, whose handler returns prisma Availability rows. Prisma models days as Int[], and getScheduleListItemData, used by ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper, requires days: number[]. The copied type declares days: string[]. A real weekday list such as [1, 2, 3] is therefore not assignable to the hook result, and a consumer that treats each day as a weekday name will format the wrong labels. Type days as number[] to match the Prisma select and the transformer.
findings.title: Availability days typed as strings, API returns numbers

findings.description: GetAvailableSlotsResponse is now the type useAvailableSlots assigns to GET /slots/available, which returns AvailableSlotsService._getAvailableSlots. The copied SlotInfo sets fromUser.id to string while IFromUser.id is number, and it omits userIds and notes that getSlots attaches and the calendar view spreads into CalendarAvailableTimeslots. A real OOO slot therefore has a numeric fromUser.id and may include userIds/notes, but the hook type rejects the id and hides the other fields from onTimeslotsLoaded and EventTypeCalendarViewComponent. The exported Slot replacement at line 19 also changes userIds from number[] to string[], so the same numeric host ids fail onTimeslotsLoaded. Model both types on IGetAvailableSlots (number ids, userIds, notes) instead of inventing SlotInfo.
findings.title: Copied slot response drops fields the API returns

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme, testCheckSystemThemeChanges reads AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.darkThemeView and expects its accessibility value to be "1". ThemeOptionView marks only the selected option as 1, and the light and dark options are mutually exclusive, so a successful light selection leaves darkThemeView at "0" and this XCTAssertEqual fails. Read lightThemeView instead, matching SelectLightTheme and the sibling dark/automatic assertions.
findings.title: Light theme assertion reads dark option

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme taps lightThemeView, the test reads darkThemeView's accessibility value and expects "1". GenericImageOption sets that value to "1" only for the selected option, so lightThemeView is "1" and darkThemeView is "0". XCTAssertEqual therefore fails on the light-theme step even when light mode is correctly selected. Restore the query to AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.lightThemeView.
findings.title: Light theme assertion checks dark theme button

findings.description: `POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite` is decorated `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")`. `RolesGuard.hasMinimumRole` treats a lower index as sufficient, and `TEAM_ROLES` is `[OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER]`, so any accepted team member passes. The parallel org invite route requires `TEAM_ADMIN`, and `createInviteHandler` allows only OWNER/ADMIN (`team.invite`). A regular MEMBER can therefore mint a shareable team-join token. Require `TEAM_ADMIN`.
findings.title: Team members can mint invite links

findings.description: The new-token path returns newToken.identifier (`invite-link-for-teamId-<teamId>`) while inviteLink is built from the random token column. POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and viewer.teams.createInvite therefore hand callers a data.token that verificationToken.findUnique({ where: { token } }) and inviteMemberByToken cannot match. The existing-token branch still returns existingToken.token, so a freshly created invite and a retrieved invite disagree. Return the created token column, not identifier.
findings.title: New invite returns identifier instead of secret token

findings.description: `buildInviteLink` changed `if (!isOrgContext)` to `if (isOrgContext)` and still returns `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=...` in that branch. A regular team (`parentId` null, `isOrganization` false) therefore gets `${WEBAPP_URL}/signup?token=<secret>&callbackUrl=...`. Signup loads the verification token by that secret and treats `identifier` as an email; the stored identifier is `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`, so signup redirects to the verification-token error page. An organization or org-subteam invite gets `/teams?token=<secret>`, which calls `inviteMemberByToken` and creates a provisional membership instead of the signup/onboarding flow. Restore `if (!isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink`.
findings.title: Invite URL branch is inverted for org vs team

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, and every call site uses `?` inside prepare_tools, which returns crate::Result. crate::Error has #[from] for std::io::Error but no From<FileWriteError> (and no FileWriteError variant). The previous signature returned std::io::Result, which converted via Error::IoError. This does not compile. Either return std::io::Result again or add a thiserror #[from] variant on the public Error enum.
findings.failureMode: ? cannot convert the new error type, so the bundler crate fails to compile
findings.title: FileWriteError does not convert to crate::Error

findings.description: The GTK install condition was flipped from `if !gtk.exists()` to `if gtk.exists()` while the body now writes the inlined script. On a normal cache (the file is absent), the branch is skipped, so linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never created. bundle_project always passes `--plugin gtk`, so linuxdeploy cannot find the plugin and AppImage bundling fails. The gstreamer block immediately below still uses `if !gstreamer.exists()`. Change the GTK condition back to `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: inverted existence check skips writing the inlined plugin
findings.title: GTK plugin is never installed on a clean cache

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now calls fs::set_permissions before fs::write. Every caller (AppRun, linuxdeploy, gtk, gstreamer, appimage plugin) only invokes it when the destination does not exist. set_permissions on a missing path returns NotFound, so the download/inline bytes are never written and prepare_tools fails. Write the bytes first, then set mode 0o770, as the previous implementation did.
findings.failureMode: set_permissions on a nonexistent path returns NotFound before write
findings.title: chmod-before-create fails for new tool files

findings.description: prepare_tools still builds the cache path from linuxdeploy_arch, which is the unchanged typo "i383" when arch is "i686", but the download URL on this line was switched from linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage to linuxdeploy-{arch}.AppImage. For a 32-bit Linux target, arch is the triple prefix "i686". The published asset is linuxdeploy-i386.AppImage; HEAD of the new URL returns 404, and linuxdeploy-i383.AppImage also 404s. The first AppImage bundle on i686 therefore fails inside download() instead of fetching the tool. Use the published i386 token in this URL (and in the cache filename), not the raw triple prefix.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage bundling downloads a 404 URL
findings.title: 32-bit linuxdeploy download URL 404s

findings.description: FileWriteError is a new custom error enum with a manual Display impl and a manual std::error::Error impl. Repository rule 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] and #[error(...)] attributes. The crate already depends on thiserror and uses it for crate::Error. Replace the hand-written impls with thiserror (and, separately, make the type convertible at the `?` sites). Leaving the manual impls keeps the error type out of the project's structured error handling even after the conversion is fixed.
findings.failureMode: new custom error implements Display and Error by hand, violating the mandated thiserror error type
findings.title: FileWriteError bypasses thiserror

findings.description: The generated AppRun hook sets GTK_PATH to \"$APPDIR/$gtk3_libdir:/usr/lib64/gtk-3.0:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0\". gtk3_libdir is the absolute pkg-config libdir plus /gtk-3.0, so on Debian/Ubuntu the first entry becomes $APPDIR/usr/lib/<triplet>/gtk-3.0, which matches what copy_tree preserves. The two fallback entries are absolute host paths, not paths inside the AppImage. GTK searches GTK_PATH and stops using its compiled-in module directory, so a machine without /usr/lib64/gtk-3.0 and /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0 (aarch64, i386, or a relocated AppImage on a host that does not have that exact tree) does not find bundled input modules and print backends. Prefix those fallbacks with $APPDIR, or drop them and export only the copied directory.
findings.failureMode: AppImage runtime searches host multiarch paths that were not bundled under APPDIR
findings.title: GTK_PATH points at host library directories

findings.description: The workaround loop finds GTK/pixbuf modules and links them into $APPDIR/usr/lib with target ${file/\\/usr\\/lib\\//}. That substitution only strips the literal prefix /usr/lib/. On Fedora-style layouts pkg-config libdir is /usr/lib64, so a module path such as /usr/lib64/gtk-3.0/3.0.0/immodules/im-ibus.so is unchanged. ln -s then creates $APPDIR/usr/lib/im-ibus.so -> /usr/lib64/... which is an absolute host path, not the copy under $APPDIR. The previous plugin rewrote $LD_GTK_LIBRARY_PATH (which included /usr/lib64) to a relative path. Strip that library prefix, or skip the link when the replacement does not produce a relative target.
findings.failureMode: ln -s keeps an absolute /usr/lib64 path, so the bundled link resolves to the host instead of the copied module
findings.title: lib64 module symlinks point outside the AppImage

findings.description: rustfmt.toml sets max_width = 100, and rule 3 requires cargo fmt --all -- --check to pass. The new set_permissions line is 101 characters, so formatting check fails on this file. Break the map_err chain onto the next line.
findings.failureMode: changed line is 101 columns, so cargo fmt --check fails
findings.title: write_and_make_executable exceeds rustfmt max width

findings.description: tsconfig.app.json changes compilerOptions.strict from true to false. ui-v2/package.json validate:types and build both run tsc -b against this config, so the mandated strict type-checking pipeline no longer checks src/. Implicit any, unchecked indexed access, and nullability errors in application code now pass validation. Restore strict: true.
findings.title: App TypeScript strict checking is disabled

findings.description: Switching Deployment status to Proactive writes the selected event into trigger.after and leaves trigger.expect empty. EventTrigger.expects() is true for every event when expect is empty, and proactive evaluation fires on the absence of expect, not after. A user who selects Not Ready and Stays in therefore submits an automation that matches any deployment event and does not watch the chosen status. Store the status in trigger.expect for both postures, matching the work-pool and work-queue fields.
findings.title: Proactive deployment status is stored in after, not expect

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult loops with `j <= keys_result->numkeys`. keys holds only numkeys entries, so the last iteration reads keys[numkeys] and then argv at that garbage position. Any command with at least one key (GET, SET, MGET) hits this during preprocessCommand/getSlotFromCommand and can crash, or treat the garbage slot as a cross-slot error. Restore `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: out-of-bounds read crashes or mis-classifies slot on every keyed command
findings.title: Slot extraction reads one past the key list

findings.description: The new slot_buffer is allocated with malloc and written, but never read: first_slot already tracks the common slot. That violates the zmalloc/zfree rule, and any return added between malloc and the matching free leaks the buffer. Delete the buffer, or if it is kept, allocate with zmalloc and free with zfree on every path.
findings.failureMode: direct malloc bypasses Redis tracking and leaks if a later return skips free; allocation is unused on every keyed command
findings.title: Slot buffer uses malloc and is never read

findings.description: The new unstructured Task in onActionTap returns before OnboardingService.handleAction runs. Compact onboarding then posts a screen-changed accessibility notification immediately after the tap, while the page advance only happens on a later main-actor turn. A forward-card tap therefore announces the current card instead of the card the action advances to. Call handleAction directly, as the previous @MainActor closure did.
findings.title: Onboarding actions are deferred past their caller

findings.description: On iOS 17 and later, OnboardingTests.tearDown returns immediately when the test name contains testSelectBottomPlacement or when running on iPad. That return is inside the method, so app.terminate() and super.tearDown() are skipped. On iPad every OnboardingTests case, including tests that change theme, leaves the app process running and skips XCTest lifecycle cleanup. Move the skip so it only bypasses switchThemeToDarkOrLight and always terminate the app and call super.tearDown.
findings.title: Onboarding teardown returns before cleanup

findings.description: Renaming testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders removes the XCTest test prefix, so XCTest no longer discovers or runs the method. AccessibilityTestPlan still lists ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders(), which no longer exists, so that plan entry is stale and the reminders coverage is silently dropped. Restore the test prefix instead of renaming the method.
findings.title: Bookmark reminders test is no longer a test

findings.description: The public macOS pool now uses vmImage macOS-15, and this step's display name was changed to Use XCode 16.4.0, but the script on the previous line still runs sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer. The November 2025 macOS-15 image ships Xcode 16.0-16.4 and 26.x only, with 16.4 at /Applications/Xcode_16.4.app (symlink Xcode_16.4.0.app). Xcode_15.2.0.app is not present, so xcode-select exits non-zero and the public macOS job fails before the build. Change the select path to /Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app/Contents/Developer.
findings.title: Public macOS job selects missing Xcode 15.2.0

findings.description: The internal macOS pool now uses image macOS-15, and this step's display name was changed to Use XCode 16.4.0, but the script on the previous line still runs sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer. The November 2025 macOS-15 image ships Xcode 16.0-16.4 and 26.x only, with 16.4 at /Applications/Xcode_16.4.app (symlink Xcode_16.4.0.app). Xcode_15.2.0.app is not present, so xcode-select exits non-zero and the internal macOS job fails before the build. Change the select path to /Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app/Contents/Developer.
findings.title: Internal macOS job selects missing Xcode 15.2.0

findings.description: The BUILD002 error previously fired for every servicing build that dropped a baseline package reference. The changed condition adds `AND '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'`, so once Versions.props advances past patch 1 the error is never raised. Baseline.Designer.props still emits BaselinePackageReference items for current package IDs (for example Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Certificate), and IsServicingBuild is true for the whole servicing branch. A later 10.0.x servicing build can therefore remove a dependency that existed in the prior release and still succeed, producing a package whose dependency set is not a superset of the last release. The replacement is not visible elsewhere in the diff. Restore the previous condition so BUILD002 applies to every servicing patch, not only patch 1.
findings.title: BUILD002 servicing check disabled after patch 1

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, and every call site uses `?` inside prepare_tools, which returns crate::Result. FileWriteError is a private manual Error type with no From/Into implementation for crate::Error, so those `?` conversions do not compile. The function should keep returning std::io::Result (or another type crate::Error already converts from) instead of introducing an unconvertible error enum.
findings.title: FileWriteError cannot convert into bundler Result

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now calls set_permissions before fs::write. On the first install of AppRun, linuxdeploy, or a plugin, the path does not exist, so set_permissions returns NotFound and prepare_tools aborts before any bytes are written. The previous order wrote the file first, then applied mode 0o770; that order must be restored.
findings.title: Executable write sets permissions before the file exists

findings.description: prepare_tools now writes the inlined GTK plugin only when linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh already exists. On a clean tools cache the file is absent, so the required gtk plugin is never installed and linuxdeploy's --plugin gtk invocation fails or bundles without GTK resources. The condition should be `if !gtk.exists()`, matching the gstreamer branch and the previous download path.
findings.title: GTK plugin is never installed on a clean cache

findings.description: The linuxdeploy download URL was changed from linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage to linuxdeploy-{arch}.AppImage. For a 32-bit target, arch is the target triple prefix i686, but the published asset is linuxdeploy-i386.AppImage. prepare_tools therefore requests a nonexistent URL and the download fails. Restore linuxdeploy_arch in this URL. The unchanged local filename mapping i686 to i383 is pre-existing and is not part of this fix.
findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL no longer matches published assets

findings.description: The inlined plugin replaces copy_lib_tree with copy_tree for GTK modules and drops the library-prefix rewrite. On Debian/Ubuntu, pkg-config libdir is /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, so modules land in AppDir/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0. The generated hook sets GTK_PATH to that same unrewritten AppDir path plus only the host directories /usr/lib64/gtk-3.0 and /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0. The previously downloaded script normalized the copy and GTK_PATH to AppDir/usr/lib/gtk-3.0, which is what AppImage runtime library lookup expects. Restore that rewrite so bundled modules are loaded from the AppImage rather than the host.
findings.title: GTK modules are copied outside the AppImage lib root

findings.description: The pixbuf install now uses copy_tree and exports the unrewritten pkg-config cache path. On multiarch hosts that path is under /usr/lib/<triplet>/..., so both the copied loaders and GDK_PIXBUF_MODULE_FILE point at AppDir/usr/lib/<triplet>/... The previously downloaded plugin rewrote that prefix to AppDir/usr/lib before the copy, cache write, and hook export. Restore that rewrite so the AppImage runtime finds the bundled loaders.cache instead of falling back to the host cache.
findings.title: Pixbuf loaders are copied without the library-path rewrite

findings.description: The workaround that links GTK/pixbuf modules into AppDir/usr/lib only strips the literal prefix /usr/lib/. On a multiarch path /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0/... the substitution yields x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0/..., which does not exist under AppDir/usr/lib; a /usr/lib64/... path is not stripped and remains an absolute host path. The previously downloaded script first rewrote the detected library prefix, producing gtk-3.0/... and using ln -sf. Strip that actual library prefix and replace existing links.
findings.title: Module symlinks miss multiarch library paths

findings.description: get_pkgconf_variable exits when a variable is absent and no default is supplied. The inlined script calls it for gtk+-3.0 exec_prefix, libdir, and gtk_binary_version, and for the gdk-pixbuf binarydir/cache/moduledir variables, without the defaults the previously downloaded script passed (/usr, the detected library path, 3.0.0, and the gdk-pixbuf 2.10.0 fallback paths). On a system whose .pc file omits one of those variables, the plugin aborts under set -e instead of continuing. Restore those default arguments.
findings.title: GTK pkg-config lookups abort without upstream fallbacks

findings.description: The generated AppRun hook detects the theme with `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme`. The previously downloaded plugin queries the Freedesktop color-scheme portal and org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme. On a current GNOME session where gtk-theme is unset, this call fails and the pipeline selects GTK_THEME_VARIANT=light, so a dark session starts as Adwaita:light. Restore the color-scheme detection.
findings.title: Bundled GTK hook uses the removed gtk-theme key

findings.description: DifyNodeFactory.__init__ always builds CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer(code_executor) when no renderer is injected. code_executor defaults to None and is only normalized on the previous line into self._code_executor. The renderer treats a passed None as an explicit executor (`code_executor or CodeExecutor` is skipped) and stores None. Every production DifyNodeFactory() call then creates template-transform nodes whose render_template does None.execute_workflow_code_template, raising AttributeError. That exception is not TemplateRenderError, so the node fails instead of rendering. Pass self._code_executor, not the raw optional argument.
findings.title: Default template renderer stores a None executor

findings.description: The updated suite still constructs TemplateTransformNode(..., graph=mock_graph, ...). The new constructor only accepts id, config, graph_init_params, graph_runtime_state, and keyword-only template_renderer, so every test raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'graph'. The newly added tests copy the same call, including test_run_with_boolean_values at this line and the pre-existing tests that this diff left unchanged. Remove the graph argument from every TemplateTransformNode construction in this file.
findings.title: Template tests pass removed graph argument

findings.description: The members API now requires ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link, but the implementation is still MagicLink.js. Loading the members API throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and member authentication cannot initialize. Restore the require to ../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink until that file is renamed.
findings.failureMode: startup failure when the members API loads
findings.title: Members API cannot load MagicLink

findings.description: The wrapper now requires ../email-service/email-event-storage, but the module remains EmailEventStorage.js. Initializing email analytics therefore throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND before event storage can be constructed. Restore the require to ../email-service/EmailEventStorage until that file is renamed.
findings.failureMode: startup failure when email analytics initializes
findings.title: Email analytics cannot load event storage

findings.description: The wrapper now requires ../email-service/email-event-processor, but the module remains EmailEventProcessor.js. Email analytics initialization throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND before the processor is created. Restore the require to ../email-service/EmailEventProcessor until that file is renamed.
findings.failureMode: startup failure when email analytics initializes
findings.title: Email analytics cannot load event processor

findings.description: DifyNodeFactory stores code_executor or CodeExecutor, but builds the default template renderer from the raw code_executor argument. A caller that injects only code_executor therefore gets code nodes on the injected executor and template-transform nodes on the real CodeExecutor, because None is passed through and the renderer substitutes CodeExecutor. Build the default renderer from self._code_executor.
findings.title: Factory drops injected code executor for templates

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc 6 but is passed seven objects: HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, and the computed value. The variadic loop stops after the field, so the value is never stored and is leaked by the following decrRefCount. The propagated command is therefore `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field`. HSETEX arity is -6, so a replica or AOF reload rejects it as the wrong number of arguments and never applies the increment. The master has already updated the field, so replicas diverge and AOF restart loses the write. Change the count to 7 so the value is included.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT rewrite drops the new field value

findings.description: The local hashTypeSet call dropped HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL and now passes only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE. For LISTPACK_EX, hashTypeSet then calls listpackExUpdateExpiry with HASH_LP_NO_TTL; for a hashtable it calls hfieldPersist. Either path removes an existing field expiry before the command returns. HINCRBY still preserves TTL, and the new replication rewrite claims KEEPTTL, but that rewrite never restores the primary's already-cleared expiry. After HSETEX key EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT key f1 1.1, HTTL returns -1 on the master instead of the remaining TTL. Restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this hashTypeSet call.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT clears field TTL on the primary

findings.description: A normal reader-mode toolbar tap dispatches GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, but handleShowReaderModeAction now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction instead of .readerMode. BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions maps that case to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which creates a reading-list record and shows the add-to-reading-list toast, rather than toggleReaderMode(). Tapping the reader-mode button therefore adds the page to the reading list and does not enable or disable reader mode. Restore displayView: .readerMode in this handler.
findings.title: Reader-mode tap adds to reading list

findings.description: cancelEditMode now keeps the selected tab URL when currentURL.isWebPage() || currentURL.isReaderModeURL. A reader-mode page URL such as http://localhost:<port>/reader-mode/page?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com is an http webpage, so the first clause keeps the raw internal URL and the second clause is redundant. handleCancelEditAction stores that URL, and LocationView then formats config.url?.absoluteString. Because URL.host drops the port, isReaderModeURL is true and displayURL would have decoded the original page, but this path bypasses displayURL. Cancelling edit while reader mode is active therefore replaces the address-bar text with the raw localhost reader-mode URL. Restore the exclusion of reader-mode URLs, or pass currentURL.displayURL.
findings.title: Cancel edit shows raw reader-mode URL

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry now sets isReaderModeEnabled to false when readerModeState is .available and true otherwise, then passes it as isEnabled to readerModeButtonTapped. The metric extra `enabled` records whether reader mode was opened or closed. On a tap while reader mode is available, the recorded enabled extra is false even though the tap opens reader mode; when reader mode is already active, the extra is true even though the tap closes it. The existing test only covers the default unavailable state, where the swapped argument mapping still yields enabled == false, so it does not catch this. Restore .available -> true and default -> false.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: tsconfig.app.json changes strict from true to false. This is the config used by the validate:types script (tsc -b --noEmit) and the production build (tsc -b), so strict null, function-type, and property checks no longer run for ui-v2/src. The mandate requires strict mode to stay enabled and type checking to remain in that validation pipeline. Restore \"strict\": true.
findings.title: App TypeScript strict checking is disabled

findings.description: Switching Deployment status to Proactive rebinds the status select from trigger.expect to trigger.after and writes only the selected event into after. The server treats after as a start condition and fires a Proactive trigger when expect events are absent. With expect left empty, an empty expect matches every event, so the automation fires only when no events arrive instead of when the deployment does not stay in the selected status. The existing mapper also sets expect to the opposite status (ready <-> not-ready) while putting the selected status in after. Fix: on Proactive, store the selected status in after and the opposite deployment status in expect, and clear the unused field when posture changes.
findings.title: Proactive deployment status never watches the selected event

findings.description: Work pool status always writes the selected event to trigger.expect, including when posture is Proactive. The server fires Proactive triggers when fewer than threshold expect events arrive, and the existing work-pool mapper puts the selected status in after and every other status in expect. Selecting Ready and Stays in therefore creates a trigger that fires when the pool does not become Ready, and after stays empty so evaluation starts immediately rather than after entering Ready. Fix: for Proactive, set after to the selected status event and expect to the other current work-pool status events.
findings.title: Work pool Proactive trigger watches the status it should stay in

findings.description: Work queue status always writes the selected event to trigger.expect, including when posture is Proactive. The server fires Proactive triggers when expect events are absent, and the existing work-queue mapper puts the selected status in after and all other statuses in expect. Selecting Paused and Stays in therefore fires when the queue does not become Paused, instead of when it leaves Paused and stays in another status. Fix: for Proactive, set after to the selected status event and expect to the other work-queue status events.
findings.title: Work queue Proactive trigger watches the status it should stay in
